author: Limbach123

title: Stay Away – An Expensive Subscription For A Worse ChatGPT
body:
MindFlow AI markets itself as a specialized ADHD and task-management coach, but in reality it is just a simple chat interface running on what feels like an outdated OpenAI model. Many of the heavily advertised features simply do not exist.

The app is extremely minimal: You are always thrown back into the same chat interface, chats are not properly saved, there is no real history and therefore no meaningful long-term learning or personalized adaptation. To-do lists only exist as plain text inside the chat: Nothing you can check off, no structured overview, no boards. Reminders or notifications for tasks: Not available. For a product that claims to support people with ADHD, this completely misses the point. On top of that: The app often responds very slowly and has already frozen on me multiple times while handling tasks.

Particularly misleading is the so-called progress system: You appear to gain experience points and “level up”, but in practice it all feels extremely generic, follows a fixed template, and is barely personalized – more cosmetic than genuinely helpful. This might work as a very rough starting point if you have absolutely no idea how to structure yourself and you are fine working only inside a chat. For almost everyone else, it will be largely useless.

In the end, MindFlow AI is simply a worse, more limited version of ChatGPT behind a paywall. No real added value, but fewer options.

The lack of a proper free trial and the fact that you are pushed straight into a subscription makes it look like a very transparent cash grab: The less you can test beforehand, the more likely you are to pay once and regret it afterwards. That is exactly how I feel: I would like my money back.

Conclusion: Practically useless for serious task management or ADHD support. Clear verdict: Stay away.
